newsitem.title: FRANCE: Schneider seeks US listing, maybe in '98.
newsitem.headline: Schneider seeks US listing, maybe in '98.

text.p: The chairman of French electrical distribution company Schneider said on Wednesday the group wants to list its shares on the New York stock market as early as next year.

"We have already begun to prepare the harmonisation of our accounting methods to conform with U.S. standards before tackling a New York quotation, which we would like to realise as soon as possible, that is to say, an objective of 1998 is something I would like to see," Didier Pineau-Valencienne told a news conference.
Schneider can now undertake the New York listing as it has sold construction company Spie Batignolles, which had prevented a clear view of Schneider's accounts, he said.
Spie and Schneider were in two very different businesses and analysts could not run their "benchmarking" analyses on Schneider as long as Spie was "polluting" the accounts, he said.

Pineau-Valencienne said he wanted Schneider to be "like a big American or British company, without a group of core shareholders", and the company should be totally open and judged on the stock markets on its merits.

Schneider stock was already one of the most liquid and internationally-held shares on the Paris market, with anything between 500,000 and one million shares traded each day between London and Paris, he said.
Some 79 percent of the capital is in public hands, with U.S., British, German and Japanese funds holding the shares.

Hungarian-born financier George Soros holds just over one percent of Schneider and had told Pineau-Valenciennes that each time there was bad publicity about the company, he bought the shares. Soros had made a lot of money on the stock, he said.

The company is inviting new members to its board, drawn from Germany, Italy, Switzerland and Britain, as part of its aim of opening up the company. It is looking for senior U.S. and Asian executives to join the board, but had encountered difficulties in finding a Japanese manager under 68 years, the statutory retirement age, he said.
Schneider earlier reported 1996 net attributable profit up 61.6 percent at 1.32 billion francs. The market consensus had been for a net profit of 1.25 billion.
The shares were up 6.36 percent at 321 francs at 1419 GMT, on turnover of 1.26 million shares.
